channel.title: Dear Mr. Librarian
channel.description: Reader questions about the translation — a word-choice, the text, the canon, a comparison between versions — answered one at a time, the way everything in this project is done: sourced, compared, and left for you to weigh rather than settled from the desk.

item.title: Did archaeologists just find Noah's Ark? What the new dig near Ararat actually found
item.description: A university-led team just wrapped a 90-day season at Turkey's Durupınar formation — soil cores, ground-penetrating radar, and carbon readings 40% higher inside than out, but no dated wood yet. What was actually reported, the site's contested 65-year back-and-forth, and why this project's own translator's note already warns about "the mountain."

item.title: What is Yom Kippur, and what does the Bible actually call the Day of Atonement?
item.description: Leviticus 16 and 23 lay out one ritual, on one day a year, that no high priest has performed in almost two thousand years — the goat English calls a "scapegoat," the penalty for skipping the fast, what changed the day the ritual's one required room stopped existing, and how a war and a legend both attached themselves to the day afterward.

item.title: Why don't Jehovah's Witnesses accept blood transfusions — and what just changed?
item.description: The Governing Body's September 18, 2026 announcement, the two Bible texts the whole position rests on, 81 years of gradual change before this one, and what bloodless surgery actually owes to this community.

item.title: Are we living in the Great Tribulation right now?
item.description: Matthew 24's actual list of signs, four ways Christians have read when it applies, and Jesus's own repeated warnings against reading your own moment as the decisive one.

item.title: Could anyone alive today be descended from Cain?
item.description: Cain's line simply stops in Genesis 4; Seth's runs to Noah; and Genesis 9:19 says the whole earth was peopled from Noah's sons. What that adds up to — and the two questions it depends on.

item.title: Did Isaac Newton write about the Bible?
item.description: The scientist wrote more on Scripture than on physics — his Daniel & Revelation, his textual criticism of the Johannine Comma, his chronology, and his hidden anti-Trinitarianism, handled honestly.

item.title: How long were the days of creation?
item.description: The elastic Hebrew word yom, the sunless first days and the open seventh, and the ordinary-day, day-age, and literary-framework readings — with their pedigrees, no vote cast.

item.title: Why does this translation say “Jehovah”?
item.description: The name of God — the four letters behind “the LORD,” why almost every Bible hides it, and the choice between “the LORD,” “Yahweh,” and “Jehovah.”

item.title: Was the Word "God," or "a god"?
item.description: John 1:1 and the deity of Christ — the Greek of the missing article, “firstborn of all creation,” the Angel of Jehovah, and the whole argument laid out on both sides.

item.title: Why isn't the Book of Enoch in this translation?
item.description: The Masoretic source text, the canon question, the Ethiopian exception, and the Dead Sea Scrolls.
